newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- Feb 13.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:

** An official Indian team headed by petroleum secretary Vijay Kelkar is leaving for Iran and Pakistan later this week to discuss the India-Iran natural gas pipeline project, the Observer newspaper reports
** The new export-import policy scheduled to be announced on March 31 will emphasise export promotion rather than import liberalisation, commerce minister B.B. Ramaiah says
** Congress Party suffers a major setback as its high-profile candidate Kamalnath lost to the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate in the Chiindwara parliamentary constitutency

** State-run Unit Trust of India (UTI), the country's largest mutual fund, plans to set up three asset management companies to manage its 69 mutual fund schemes, the Financial Express newspaper reports
UTI also plans to enter the insurance industry and is expected to announce a tie up with an overseas firm - most likely Commercial Union of U.K., the paper says
** The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) plans a 10-billion rupee private placement of bonds to institutional and high net worth individuals, the Economic Times reports
** The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share benchmark index ended Wednesday 0.54 percent lower at 3,483.48.
** The National Stock Exchange closed above the BSE prices at start of weekly account on Wednesday, index closing up by 8.25 points to 1,001.0.
** Indian stocks very attractive at present, chairman of Morgan Stanley Group, quoted as saying in the Business Standard
